Political

puh-LIT-ih-kuhl · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Political is relating to government and how a country or area is run.

Election posters made the whole street feel political in November.

Worked Example

The two candidates had a political debate about fixing the town's roads.

The debate is about how the town should be run - its roads and its leaders. Questions like that are political.

How Political Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

governmental

governmental: about government

civic

civic: about citizens and their community

Antonyms

nonpolitical

nonpolitical: having nothing to do with government

How Strong Is It? — Civic → political → Governmental

Civic vs. political

Civic vs. political: Civic is milder: a civic project, like a park cleanup, helps the community without picking sides.

Governmental vs. political

Governmental vs. political: Governmental is stronger and more formal: a governmental decision comes straight from the people in charge.

The pieces

root — politic

root — politic: city, citizens (Greek (polis))

suffix — al

suffix — al: characteristic of, relating to (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Politic- comes from polis, the Greek word for city, so political describes how cities and countries are run.

Use the root in a new word: police

Use the root in a new word: police: The police officer helped us cross the busy street - police comes from the same ancient city root as political!
